question.problem: What is the domain of the function $f(x)=\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{x}{2}+{60}^{∘}),$ where $x$ is measured in degrees? Assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.worked_solution:
The domain of $y=\operatorname{sec}⁡x$ consists of all values where $\operatorname{cos}⁡x\ne 0,$ and is given by the expression

$$
x\ne {90}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘},
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the domain of $\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{x}{2}+{60}^{∘}),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(\frac{x}{2}+{60}^{∘}).$ This gives

$$
\frac{x}{2}+{60}^{∘}\ne {90}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}.
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2}+{60}^{∘} & \ne {90}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘} \\ \frac{x}{2} & \ne {90}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}-{60}^{∘} \\ \frac{x}{2} & \ne {30}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘} \\ x & \ne {60}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of the function is $x\ne {60}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘},$ where $n$ is an integer.
